name: MySpace
blurb: The 2000s social network of Tom, Top 8 friends and profile songs
title: What Happened to MySpace? Tom, Top 8 and the Lost Music
description: MySpace was the mid-2000s social network, launched in 2003 and the most visited US site in 2006 before Facebook overtook it. It still exists, mostly dormant.
answer: MySpace was a social network launched in August 2003 where you decorated your own profile, picked a song to autoplay and ranked your Top 8 friends. News Corporation bought it for $580 million in 2005, and in June 2006 it was the most visited website in the US, but Facebook overtook it in 2008 and it was sold for about $35 million in 2011. The site still exists under the ad-tech company Viant, which lost most music and photos uploaded before 2016 in a server migration that MySpace confirmed in March 2019, and has said it plans a relaunch, with no date.

body: A MySpace profile was a page you could make your own. Users pasted HTML and CSS code into the "About Me" and "Interests" boxes to change the background, colors and layout, which is why so many pages had glittery wallpaper, clashing fonts and blinking images. A favorite song could play the moment someone opened your page, and bands used the site to post their music.

Every new account came with one friend already added: Tom Anderson, the co-founder and the site's first president. Your Top 8 sat at the top of your page, and choosing who made the list, and in what order, was a small social drama.

head: Year
What happened
rows: MySpace launches in August, built by employees of the internet company eUniverse; Chris DeWolfe and Tom Anderson are its founders
News Corporation buys it in July for $580 million
In June it passes Yahoo Mail and Google Search as the most visited website in the US
Peaks at about 115 million monthly visitors in April; Facebook passes it in Alexa's rankings the same month
Sold to Specific Media and Justin Timberlake for about $35 million
Time Inc. buys MySpace and its parent company
A botched server migration wipes out songs, photos and videos uploaded before 2016; Meredith sells MySpace to Viant in November

body: In March 2019 MySpace confirmed that, "as a result of a server migration project", photos, videos and audio uploaded more than three years earlier might no longer be available. Users had noticed old songs refusing to play since early 2018. The widely cited estimate of more than 50 million songs from 14 million artists came from outside the company, not from MySpace itself, which said the files were corrupted and could not be recovered. In April 2019 the Internet Archive recovered about 490,000 of the lost MP3s.

Yes, the site is still online, but it has been largely inactive for years and much of its old media no longer works. Its owners, the brothers who run Viant Technology, said in a 2026 documentary that they still own MySpace and intend to relaunch it when the time is right; no date or design has been announced. Tom Anderson was replaced as president in 2009 and now works as a landscape photographer.

ul: "Tom" in everyone's friend list, which made "Tom from MySpace" a nickname
Rearranging your Top 8 after a falling-out with a friend
Copying layout code from fan sites to get a new background
Bands posting songs and tour dates on their own MySpace pages

faq.a: Tom Anderson, a co-founder and the site's first president. He was added automatically as every new user's first friend until about 2010.

faq.q: Can I get my old MySpace photos and songs back?
faq.a: Most files uploaded before 2016 were lost in a server migration that MySpace confirmed in March 2019, and the company said they cannot be recovered. Only a small archived set of songs survived elsewhere.
Facebook overtook it in 2008 and kept growing while MySpace lost users and value; in 2011 it sold for about $35 million, a fraction of what News Corporation had paid.
